paper.title: Streaming kernel regression with provably adaptive mean, variance, and regularization

settings.name_in_paper: Kernelized bandits with unknown noise variance (Kernel UCB)
unmapped: Noise variance sigma^2 unknown; learner knows a loose upper bound sigma_+ >= sigma and a lower bound sigma_- <= sigma
Learner knows an upper bound C on the RKHS norm ||f_star||_K (recorded as S)
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t \geq 1$, a bandit algorithm recommends a point $x_t$ to sample and observes a noisy outcome $y_t = f_\star(x_t) + \xi_t$, where $\xi_t \sim \Normal(0, \sigma^2)$. ... minimizes the cumulative regret $\kR_T = \sum_{t=1}^T f_\star(\star) - f_\star(x_t)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Kernelized bandits with unknown noise variance, discrete arm set (Kernel TS)
unmapped: Noise variance sigma^2 unknown; learner knows a loose upper bound sigma_+ >= sigma and a lower bound sigma_- <= sigma
Learner knows an upper bound C on the RKHS norm ||f_star||_K (recorded as S)
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the set of arms $\bX$ is \emph{discrete}. ... observes a noisy outcome $y_t = f_\star(x_t) + \xi_t$, where $\xi_t \sim \Normal(0, \sigma^2)$.

algorithms.name: Kernel UCB with unknown variance and adaptive regularization
Kernel TS with adaptive variance estimation and regularization tuning (Algorithm 1)

symbols.sigma_plus: known upper bound sigma_+ >= sigma on the noise standard deviation
symbols.gamma_sig: information gain gamma_T(sigma^2/C^2) = 1/2 sum_t ln(1 + k_{lambda,t-1}(x_t,x_t)/lambda) with lambda = sigma^2/C^2

tuning: lambda_t = sigma_{+,t}^2/C^2 adapted online via Corollary 3.1

source.label: thm:KernelUCB
source.quote: With probability higher than $1-\delta$, the regret of Kernel UCB with adaptive regularization and variance estimation satisfies for all $T\geq0$ ... $\kR_T \leq 2\sum_{t=1}^T\sqrt{\frac{k_{\lambda_t,t-1}(x_t,x_t)}{\lambda_t}} B_{\lambda_t,t-1}(\delta/4)$. In particular, we have $\kR_T \leq 2\frac{\sigma_+}{\sigma}\Big(1 + \sqrt{2\ln(4/\delta) + 2 \gamma_T(\sigma_{-}^2/C^2)}\big)C \sqrt{T \frac{2\gamma_T(\sigma^2/C^2) }{\ln(1 + C^2/\sigma^2)} }$.

results.notes: Regret is sum of f_star gaps (realized pseudo-regret) holding w.p. 1-delta uniformly over T. gamma_T here is the data-dependent information gain on the played points, not the max information gain. Paper's C is the RKHS norm bound (mapped to S). Lemma 4.1 requires lambda_t >= sigma^2/C^2, which holds w.h.p.

bound.expression_latex: C_{1,T}\frac{\sigma_+}{\sigma}\Big( 1 +\sqrt{2\ln(4/\delta) + 2 \gamma_T(\sigma_-^2/C^2)} \Big)  C\sqrt{T \frac{2 \gamma_T(\sigma^2/C^2)}{\ln(1 + C^2/\sigma^2)}} +C_2 R\sqrt{T \ln(1/\delta)} + 4\pi e R \delta

symbols.gamma_sig: information gain gamma_T(sigma^2/C^2) on the played points
symbols.R_max: maximal instantaneous pseudo-regret max_x f_star(star) - f_star(x)

source.label: thm:kernel_ts
source.quote: Assume that the maximal instantaneous pseudo-regret $R=\max_{x\in\bX}\big(f_\star(\star)-f_\star(x)\big)$ is finite. Then, the regret of Kernel TS (Algorithm~\ref{alg:kernel_ts}) with $v_t = \frac{B_{\lambda_t,t-1}(\delta/4)}{\sigma_{+,t-1}}$ after $T$ episodes is $\cO(C \sqrt{T \ln(T |\bX|)} \gamma_T(\sigma^2/C^2))$ with probability $1 - 3 \delta$. ... Further, we have $\kR_T \leq C_{1,T}\frac{\sigma_+}{\sigma}\Big( 1 +\sqrt{2\ln(4/\delta) + 2 \gamma_T(\sigma_-^2/C^2)} \Big)  C\sqrt{T \frac{2 \gamma_T(\sigma^2/C^2)}{\ln(1 + C^2/\sigma^2)}} +C_2 R\sqrt{T \ln(1/\delta)} + 4\pi e R \delta$.

results.notes: Holds w.p. 1-3delta for all T. C_{1,T} expanded inline with |X| = K. The theorem also states a summary O(C sqrt(T ln(T|X|)) gamma_T(sigma^2/C^2)); not recorded separately since it is a loose restatement whose exact derivation from the explicit bound is unclear.
